 Updated: 2:10 PM PST Nov 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Brian Wiechert Digital Content Manager Breakfast sandwiches, whipped cream and bicycle helmets are among the latest products recalled across the nation. 
 Several companies have pulled products from stores or warned consumers about potential safety risks, affecting everything from cars and SUVs, air-fryer ovens, children’s pajamas, infant bouncers and magnetic toys. 
 Advertisement Related video above | Check your fridge: Recalled foods could already be in your home 
 Some involve undeclared allergens or bacteria that can cause serious illness. Others raise concerns about fires, burns, falls or entrapment. 
 Here’s what to know about the affected products recalled over the past few weeks, the risks and where they were sold. 
 FOOD ITEMS
 Whipped cream. A batch of Kirkland Signature Real Heavy Whipped Cream may contain a small amount of cleaning chemical; affected 15-ounce cans have a best-by date of April 2, 2027, and can timestamps from 00:35 to 02:45. Costco sold it in 12 states: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Wisconsin. Click here to view the full recall 
 Breakfast biscuit sandwiches. Grand Strand Sandwich Company recalled four Lunch Box varieties—bacon, egg and cheese; jumbo sausage; sausage, egg and cheese; and chicken sausage biscuits—because they may be contaminated with Listeria. They were sold in convenience stores, vending machines and prison canteens in North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia. Click here to view the full recall 
 Frozen dessert bars. Naia recalled Chocolate Banana Bar Sorbetto with specified date codes after some pistachio gelato bars were put in wrappers that did not declare pistachio, milk or egg. The bars were sold in Northern California and Reno, Nevada. Click here to view the full recall 
 Refrigerated pasta. ALDI recalled Priano Protein Carbonara Tortelloni and Protein Herb & Cheese Tortelloni because they may have been kept at improper temperatures and could contain botulism-causing bacteria. The products were sold at ALDI stores in Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina and South Carolina. Click here to view the full recall 
 Cheddar cheese. Family Farmstead Dairy recalled its raw mild cheddar cheese because it may be contaminated with E. coli. The affected cheese was distributed through retailers in Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania and Virginia. Click here to view the full recall 
 Breakfast biscuit sandwiches. Fresh & Ready Foods recalled Fresh to You sausage, egg and cheese biscuit sandwiches because they may be contaminated with Listeria. The recalled sandwiches were made at the company’s Longview, Texas facility; check the notice for the affected distribution details. Click here to view the full recall 
 MEDICATIONS 
 Blood pressure medication. Breckenridge Pharmaceutical recalled one lot of 60-mg extended-release propranolol capsules because of possible metal contamination that could cause cuts to the mouth or digestive tract. The lot was distributed to wholesalers and pharmacies nationwide. Click here to view the full recall 
 Dried herbal root. Larbi recalled three lots of Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root C/S in 4-ounce pouches because they may be contaminated with Salmonella. The product was sold nationwide through the company website, online marketplaces and retail stores. Click here to view the full recall 
 Dietary supplement capsules. bioQuad Life Sciences issued an allergy alert for OsteoDenx capsules because the product contains undeclared milk, which may cause a serious reaction in people with milk allergies. Click here to view the full recall 
 Medical beds and accessories. Medline’s recall and repair-or-replace program covers Medline-brand beds, rails, mattresses and accessories because electrical parts can overheat and cause fires, while some bed-and-accessory setups can create entrapment or asphyxiation risks. The products were distributed in the United States and Canada. Click here to view the full recall 
 EVERYDAY ITEMS
 Air-fryer ovens. Gourmia recalled its stainless-steel 9-slice digital air-fryer ovens, model GTF7530, because the glass doors can swing shut unexpectedly and burn someone retrieving food. The ovens were sold at Target stores nationwide and online. Click here to view the full recall 
 Adult portable bed rails. Xentrawave recalled XT016 rails from all batches and XT026 rails from batch 20251212 because users can become trapped between a rail and mattress and suffocate; one death was reported. The rails were sold in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Bicycle helmets. Cipton recalled white youth-size helmets with built-in multicolored LED strips because they fail impact, stability and certification requirements and may not protect a rider in a crash. They were sold at Dick’s Sporting Goods and JCPenney stores nationwide and online. Click here to view the full recall 
 Rechargeable battery packs. Ororo recalled PD10K-Pro lithium-ion packs because they can overheat and cause fires or burns; one overheating report was received. The packs were sold online at Ororowear.com and Amazon in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Magnetic robot toys. CHE-US recalled magnetic stick-figure robot toys sold in sets of five or 10 because magnets can come loose when the figures are pulled apart and pose a serious ingestion hazard. They were sold on Amazon.com in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Children’s pajamas. Qpancy recalled children’s pajama sets because they do not meet federal sleepwear flammability standards, creating a burn risk. The sets were sold online in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Waterproof dry bags. Fidlock recalled medium Hermetic dry bags because their adhesive closure strips can detach and release magnets that could be swallowed. The affected bags were sold in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Infant bouncers. Kidsview recalled khaki bouncers made in August, September or October 2022 because they can collapse during use and injure an infant. They were sold online in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Electric off-highway vehicles. Vanderhall recalled model-year 2024–2026 Brawley GTS vehicles because the brakes may engage while airborne and lock up when the vehicle lands, risking a crash and serious injury. The recall covers vehicles sold in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 Lighted portfolios and measuring tools. Hultafors Group recalled select CLC portfolios, Johnson Level angle locators and calipers, and Calculated Industries calculators because button-cell batteries can be accessed, posing a risk of serious injury if swallowed. The products were sold in the United States. Click here to view the full recall 
 VEHICLES
 Cars, trucks and SUVs. Toyota is recalling more than 314,000 vehicles with passenger-side Takata airbags that may degrade and rupture, sending metal fragments into the cabin and potentially causing serious injury or death. The affected Toyota and Lexus models were sold in the United States; owner notices are expected to begin Dec. 28. Click here to view the full recall 
 Luxury SUVs. Ford recalled about 36,994 model-year 2025–2027 Lincoln Navigators because the front passenger seat may move unexpectedly when the rear-seat “Chauffeur Seat” feature is activated, potentially striking passengers or putting the front occupant in an unsafe position. The recall applies to vehicles in the United States. Click here to view the full recall
